What Is Palestine? Palestine is a historical term for a region that has encompassed many territories — originally named by the Romans in 135 AD, when they renamed Judea in an attempt to sever the Jewish connection to the land. Across the centuries, the land was ruled by empire after empire, yet no sovereign country called Palestine ever existed. It began as a name meant to erase a people — and the question today is whether it's still being used to do exactly that. The last episode of "What Is" Season 1 is this Thursday at 11am ET.

🇫🇷 LYON, FRANCE — WHEN PROTESTS PUT INNOCENT LIVES AT RISK “THERE ARE YOUNG PEOPLE IN THE BUILDING!” Those are the desperate words of a woman witnessing fires near residential buildings during the unrest in Lyon, France, on October 24, 2026. According to local journalist @medaveprod, firefighters were struggling to get through as fires burned in the streets. Imagine being trapped in your own home, watching flames outside while emergency responders struggle to reach you. People have every right to peacefully protest rising living costs, education conditions, and government policies. But when demonstrations turn into destruction, innocent residents are the ones left fearing for their safety. Reports indicate that approximately 10,000 people participated in Saturday's demonstrations in Lyon, with 36 arrests and 22 reported injuries. When did setting streets on fire become an acceptable form of protest? Where is the concern for families, children, elderly residents, and emergency workers? Freedom of expression matters. Peaceful protest matters. But so does public safety.
